# Références bibliographiques

## Corpus historique Drift-X (2006–2009)

1. Brun, J.-M. (2006). *Modélisation à complexité réduite de la dérive*. Thèse de doctorat, Université Montpellier II.
2. Mohammadi, B. & Brun, J.-M. (2006). [Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite](https://www.em-consulte.com/article/69927). *C. R. Mécanique* 334(10), 634–638.
3. Mohammadi, B., Brun, J.-M. & Pironneau, O. (2006). Reduced order modelling of dispersion. In *Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing with PDE and their challenging applications*, Springer.
4. Brun, J.-M. & Mohammadi, B. (2008). [Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14). In Glowinski & Neittaanmäki (eds), *Partial Differential Equations: Modelling and Numerical Simulation*, CSM vol. 16, Springer, chap. 14, p. 245 et s.
5. Bozon, N., Mohammadi, B. & Sinfort, C. (2008). Similitude and non symmetric geometry for dispersion modelling. e-sta vol. 5, STIC & Environnement'07.
6. Bozon, N., Sinfort, C. & Mohammadi, B. (2009). [A GIS-based atmospheric dispersion model (Drift-X)](https://hal.science/hal-00468863). HAL.
7. Mohammadi, B. & Bozon, N. (2009). [GIS-based atmospheric dispersion modelling](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12518-009-0006-0). *Applied Geomatics* 1, 33–39.

## Fondements méthodologiques

8. Mohammadi, B. & Pironneau, O. (2001). *Applied Shape Optimization for Fluids*. Oxford University Press. (concept de sensibilité incomplète)
9. Borouchaki, H., George, P.-L., Hecht, F., Laug, P. & Saltel, E. (1997). [Delaunay mesh generation governed by metric specifications. Part I: Algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0168-874X(96)00057-1). *Finite Elements in Analysis and Design* 25, 61–83. (lignée des métriques de l'adaptation de maillage)
10. Raupach, M. R. & Thom, A. S. (1981). Turbulence in and above plant canopies. *Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics* 13, 97–129.
11. Simpson, J. E. (1997). *Gravity Currents in the Environment and the Laboratory*. Cambridge University Press.

## État de l'art moderne (sélection)

12. Hutchinson, M., Oh, H. & Chen, W.-H. (2017). [A review of source term estimation methods for atmospheric dispersion events using static or mobile sensors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S156625351630152X). *Information Fusion* 36, 130–148.
13. U.S. EPA (2024). [Guideline on Air Quality Models — Enhancements to the AERMOD Dispersion Modeling System](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/29/2024-27636/guideline-on-air-quality-models-enhancements-to-the-aermod-dispersion-modeling-system). Federal Register.
14. U.S. EPA. [Guidance on the Use of the Linked AGDISP-Gaussian Extension Models for far field drift](https://www.epa.gov/pesticide-science-and-assessing-pesticide-risks/guidance-use-linked-agdisp-gaussian-extension).
15. AgAir Update (2026). [Bayer Crop Science joins Ag industry efforts to modernize spray drift model (AGDISP Modernization Project)](https://agairupdate.com/2026/03/09/bayer-crop-science-joins-ag-industry-efforts-to-modernize-spray-drift-model-used-by-pesticide-regulators/).
16. Ayoub, A. et al. (2024). [An enhanced Fourier neural operator surrogate for radioactive plume transport forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00477-024-02738-8). *Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment* (WSPEEDI).
17. HAL (2024). [Reduced-order model (POD-GPR) for microscale atmospheric dispersion](https://hal.science/hal-04310899/document).
18. Turbelin, G., Singh, S. K. & Issartel, J.-P. (2016). [Reconstructing source terms from atmospheric concentration measurements: the renormalization technique](https://doi.org/10.1002/2014MS000385). *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*.

La bibliographie complète, catégorisée et datée (une trentaine d'entrées), est maintenue dans le dépôt : <code>docs/references.md</code>. Les citations du site sont gérées par <code>references.bib</code>.
